note: Structured successor to DICT.txt (migrated 2026-07-24). DICT.txt is retained as historical source; all new decisions go here. Validate with: node scripts/dict-lint.js

statuses.candidate: queued for the PR1 normalization loop; rendering (if any) is provisional
statuses.decided: rendering chosen and recorded with rationale; not yet applied corpus-wide
statuses.applied: rendering imputed across every occurrence; invariant checks green

entries.rationale: R$'+ is a noun from the root RA$ (rosh, 'head') — head-part, first-in-rank-or-time. Superseded the prior 'firstfruit' rendering 2026-07-24: 'firstfruit' encoded the cultic USE of the lemma, not its sense, and read wrong in the ~29 of 49 verses that have no offering in view (GEN/1:1 'In firstfruit created Elohim'; JERM/26:1 etc. regnal accession-year; PROV/1:7, 8:22, PSLM/111:10 priority; JOB/8:7, 42:12 temporal bracket against 'latter end'). 'first' was rejected on I2 grounds: it is the natural claim of H7223 rishon (174 verses) and Greek protos (146) over this lemma's 49, and it is an adjective where R$'+ is a noun ('In first created Elohim' is worse English than the original). 'beginning' keeps the noun, is uncontested by any other decided entry, and pairs natively with the Greek arche.
notes: Firstfruit sense DROPPED, not split (human decision 2026-07-24). Genuine 'firstfruits' in the offering passages is H1061 bikkurim, which already carries that English word in the corpus — EX/23:19, EX/34:26 and EZEK/44:30 have BOTH lemmas, so those three are imputed via --ambiguous H1061 and hand-resolved.

Greek lemma deliberately omitted for now. The correct pair is arche, NOT G536 aparche: the LXX uses aparche for R$'+ only in the offering passages and arche elsewhere, and that mismatch is what dragged this entry cultic. arche needs its own PR3 split off its rule/authority sense ('principalities and powers') before it can be paired here.

grk lemma fields hold Greek script to key against MorphGNT (see the elohim entry). The prior version of this entry had "lemma": "aparche" in romanized form, which matched zero verses in data/lemmas.json — the Greek side of this entry had never actually imputed.

entries.rationale: BRA is the divine-making verb: in Biblical Hebrew the qal subject is always Elohim, never a human agent, which is precisely the distinction worth preserving (P3). The corpus inherited YLT's scattered rendering — the 'prepare' family dominates (prepared, prepareth, preparing, Preparer) with 'produced'/'Producing' alongside, and only ~9 of 46 verses already read create/Creator. 'make' and 'made' were rejected: H6213 asah already carries the make-family in 758 verses, and 'made' is the most generic making-word in English, discarding exactly the distinction being normalized. 'fashion' was rejected as belonging to H3335 yatsar — fashion presupposes material (Latin factio, a making by shaping), which is the potter's verb, whereas BRA implies no material; ISAH/43:7 and ISAH/45:18 stack bara/yatsar/asah deliberately and collapse if two of the three are shaping words. Moving BRA off 'prepare' also frees that word for H3559 kun, which legitimately wants it.
notes: SINGLE SENSE BY DECISION (human, 2026-07-25): every H1254 occurrence takes this word, conjugated per forms. The user's governing principle is consistency of verbage, which dies if one word carries multiple senses. Accepted cost — Strong's H1254 also lumps a 'cut down / clear / carve' sense and a hiphil 'fatten', so these verses now read strangely: JOSH/17:15 and JOSH/17:18 ('created for thee there', BHS ובראת / ובראתו, contextually clearing forest), EZEK/21:19 ('a station create thou', carving a signpost), EZEK/23:47 ('created them with their swords'), 1SAM/2:29 ('to create yourselves fat', hiphil להבריאכם). This is a deliberate trade of English tolerability for lemma consistency, not an oversight.
Greek deliberately unpaired in this commit — one lemma per commit (I6). The counterpart is κτίζω (13 verses, Greek script keys per the elohim entry convention), a separate PR1.
NUM/16:30 renders the noun בריאה as 'creation' (was 'a strange thing'); PSLM/89:12 was 'appointed'. Both are within sense I.

Verb entry: forms[] is populated, so impute and check-mapping match these exact forms rather than prefix-stemming. Imputed via per-form replace targets (prepared=created, prepareth=createth, preparing=creating, preparer=Creator, produced=created, producing=creating).

entries.rationale: The realm above the earth and the divine dwelling — one lexeme in both languages. YLT already 'heaven(s)' in 394/395 H8064 verses and 255/255 οὐρανός verses. Hebrew is plural-only, so the OT surfaces as 'heavens' (P5); Greek number follows οὐρανός. Pair: LXX GEN/1:1 [LXX unverified]; NT 'heaven and earth' (MATT/5:18) echoes GEN/1:1.
notes: Firmament/expanse belongs to raqia H7549 (GEN/1:6), not here; 'sky' left unowned.

senses.definition: a bounded territory — the land of a people or place, or land given/possessed
senses.adjudication: Collapse test pending (PR3.3): collapse to 'earth' reads 'the earth of Egypt'; collapse to 'land' reads GEN/1:1 'the heavens and the land'. Caveat: the choice is interpretive in GEN/6–8 (flood extent) and GEN/41:57 ('all the earth came to Egypt') — the alternate imports a reading there; a single term would not.

entries.rationale: The ground-level world as a whole (GEN/1:1) and, in construct/possessive use, a bounded territory ('land of Egypt'). YLT splits it: ~1514 of 2190 H776 verses carry 'land', ~675 'earth'; γῆ 132 'earth' / 76 'land'. Under amended P1 erets may own both terms because neither is any other lemma's: adamah H127 is entered as 'ground' to keep 'land' free. Pair: LXX GEN/1:1 [LXX unverified].
notes: Selection list for the 'land' alternate not built — required before decided (PR3.4).

entries.rationale: Tillable soil; the namesake of adam (H120, entry `adam`) — GEN/2:7 adam formed from the adamah. YLT 'ground' in 166/211 verses, but also 'land' 56 and 'earth' 24; those move to 'ground' so 'land'/'earth' stay owned by erets (I2).
notes: Greek: LXX renders adamah with γῆ too [LXX unverified]; γῆ is paired with erets, so the NT cannot echo adamah separately — annotate, don't share (I2).

senses.definition: come to be, become, come to pass — change of state or event
senses.adjudication: User decision 2026-11-06: hayah owns 'be' and 'become', selected by context. Collapse test: 'be' alone loses GEN/2:7 'man became a living soul'; 'become' alone forces stative clauses ('I become who I become', EX/3:14).

entries.rationale: The commonest verb in GEN/1:1–5 (3131 verses). Owns two terms by context (amended P1). Greek pairs bind per term: εἰμί (2094 NT verses) carries 'be', γίνομαι (625) carries 'become' — LXX GEN/1:2 ἦν, GEN/1:3 γενηθήτω/ἐγένετο [LXX unverified]. Hebrew nominal clauses have no verb: their English copula is supplied and must be marked [is], which keeps 'be' reversible.
notes: GEN/1:2 (haytah) is the crux and is deliberately NOT in assign.json: unlisted means default 'be' ('the earth was tohu and bohu'); listing it 'become' gives 'became' (the ruin–restoration reading). The default is not a decision — review GEN/1:2 explicitly before hayah is decided.
vayehi ('and it came to pass', ~800×) needs a policy: 'become' (LXX καὶ ἐγένετο) or 'be'. It is the bulk of the assign.json work.
Forms (be/is/was/were/been…, become/became…) to be listed at decision; until then stem matching cannot see irregular forms.

entries.rationale: Loan-word per P4. 19 verses; range formlessness/emptiness/vanity/waste (GEN/1:2, DEUT/32:10 wilderness, 1SAM/12:21 idols, ISAH/40:17 nations counted as tohu). No single English word covers the range without colliding: 'vanity' is hevel's (H1892, 64 verses) natural claim, 'waste' the desolation family's. Transliteration keeps all 19 linked and pairs with bohu — 'tohu-bohu' is already a loan phrase for chaos.
notes: Greek: LXX GEN/1:2 ἀόρατος [LXX unverified] — NOT paired: NT ἀόρατος means 'invisible' (COL/1:15 'image of the invisible God'). LXX equivalence is not lexical equivalence.

entries.rationale: Loan-word per P4, with tohu. 3 verses, always beside tohu: GEN/1:2, ISAH/34:11, JERM/4:23 (Jeremiah's un-creation echo of GEN/1:2 — transliteration keeps the echo, P2).
notes: Greek: LXX ἀκατασκεύαστος [LXX unverified]; absent from NT — nothing to pair.

entries.rationale: Absence of light; antonym of or (H216). YLT 'dark…' 77/77; σκότος 28/29. Pair: LXX GEN/1:2 [LXX unverified]; 2COR/4:6 ('light shall shine out of darkness') echoes GEN/1:3.
notes: σκοτία (13 NT verses, JOHN/1:5) is a separate lemma and cannot also be 'darkness' (I2) — needs its own term. araphel H6205 ('thick darkness', 15 verses) likewise.

entries.rationale: Plural-form noun 'face' (GEN/1:2 'upon the face of the abyss'). 1891 verses, mostly inside compound prepositions — lifnei (YLT 'before' ~1068), mipnei, al-pnei. P5 favours rendering those compositionally ('at the face of') so the noun stays visible. Pair: LXX GEN/1:2 [LXX unverified]; πρόσωπον 57/71 'face'.
notes: Alternative: own 'before' as an alternate — but 'before' is the natural claim of ἔμπροσθεν/ἐνώπιον/πρό, which would then need other terms. 'presence' (YLT ~161) left unowned.

entries.rationale: The primeval/subterranean deep. P3: 'abyss' is precise, English-naturalized from the very Greek that renders it (LXX GEN/1:2 [LXX unverified]), and leaves 'deep' for amoq H6013 (16 verses). YLT 'deep' 23/35. PSLM/42:7 'abyss calls to abyss'.
notes: I5: ROM/10:7 'into the abyss' reworks DEUT/30:13, whose Hebrew has yam H3220 'sea', not tehom — annotate the divergence; bend neither entry.

senses.definition: moving air as a physical agent
senses.adjudication: Collapse test pending: collapse to 'spirit' gives EX/14:21 'a strong east spirit'. Caveat: GEN/1:2 itself is contested ('spirit of Elohim' vs 'wind of/from Elohim'); selection there is interpretive.

entries.rationale: Moving air as breath/wind and as animating/divine spirit — one Hebrew lexeme. YLT splits it: 'spirit' ~235, 'wind' ~88, 'breath' ~20 of 348 verses. Amended P1 lets ruach own 'spirit' and 'wind'; 'breath' is left to neshamah H5397 (24 verses).
notes: Paired with πνεῦμα (user decision 2026-11-06: ruach/pneuma). πνεῦμα has the same spirit/wind range; YLT renders it 'spirit' in 340/344 NT verses, so the NT 'wind' alternate is new.

Merged from the retired `pneuma` entry (DICT.txt 'pneuma -> [trans?]', romanized key that matched no MorphGNT verse). Pairing settles the transliteration question in favour of the shared English terms.

assign.json proposals: GEN/8:1, EX/14:21 → wind; JOHN/3:8 → [wind, spirit] — 'the pneuma blows where it wills … born of the pneuma'. Interpretive: John's wordplay rests on the double sense; one term per occurrence forces a choice.

entries.rationale: 3 verses: GEN/1:2 (over the waters), DEUT/32:11 (eagle over her young — the echo that glosses GEN/1:2), JERM/23:9 ('all my bones flutter', Qal). 'flutter' fits all three; 'hover' fails JERM/23:9. YLT 'flutter' 3/3.
notes: Greek: LXX GEN/1:2 ἐπιφέρω [LXX unverified] — NOT paired: NT ἐπιφέρω means 'bring upon/inflict' (ROM/3:5, JUDE/1:9).

entries.rationale: Plural-only noun; YLT 'water(s)' 523/525; ὕδωρ 68 NT verses. Pair: LXX GEN/1:2 [LXX unverified].
notes: P5: Hebrew plural form → 'waters'; forms list at decision.

entries.rationale: Commonest speech verb (4337 verses). MorphGNT lemmatizes εἶπον under λέγω (1997 NT verses). YLT 'say/said/saith'. Pair: LXX GEN/1:3 εἶπεν [LXX unverified].
notes: 'speak' reserved for dabar (verb H1696) / λαλέω — not yet entered. 'said in his heart' renders compositionally; no alternate.

entries.rationale: Light (noun). YLT 109/110; φῶς 57/61. Pair: LXX GEN/1:3 [LXX unverified]; 2COR/4:6 echoes GEN/1:3.
notes: The verb or (H215, 'give light') shares the spelling 'light'; if entered, I2 forces a distinct term unless English-term identity becomes headword+part-of-speech (open question). maor H3974 is `luminary`.

entries.rationale: Perception verb (1206 verses). MorphGNT lemmatizes εἶδον/ὤφθη under ὁράω (453 NT verses). Pair: LXX GEN/1:4 εἶδεν [LXX unverified]. Niphal 'appear' (YLT ~81) is the passive — render 'be seen' (P5; GEN/1:9) rather than an alternate, leaving 'appear' for φαίνω.
notes: βλέπω (117), θεωρέω (56), θεάομαι are separate lemmas and need distinct terms (e.g. 'look', 'observe'); 'behold' is hinneh/ἰδού's natural claim.

entries.rationale: GEN/1:4 refrain 'that it is good'. 521 verses; YLT 'good' 432.
notes: Greek pair open: LXX GEN/1:4 καλός [LXX unverified], but ἀγαθός is also a major equivalent and the NT uses both (90 verses each). Only one can share 'good' with tov; the other needs a distinct term (e.g. καλός → 'fine'/'noble'). Human decision.

entries.rationale: Hiphil 'make a division' (GEN/1:4,6,14,18; LEV/20:24,26 Israel separated from the peoples). YLT 'separate' 40/40. Keeps 'divide' free for chalaq H2505. Paired with ἀφορίζω (shared definition; YLT NT 'separate' 9/9: MATT/25:32, ACTS/13:2, ROM/1:1).
notes: LXX GEN/1:4 uses διαχωρίζω [LXX unverified], absent from SBLGNT; pairing is by shared definition, not LXX equivalence.

entries.rationale: Preposition, usually doubled (GEN/1:4 'between the light and between the darkness' — P5 keeps the doubling). YLT 'between' 224/248. Paired with μεταξύ (shared definition; YLT NT 'between' 7/9).
notes: μεταξύ also means 'next/afterward' (ACTS/13:42 'the next sabbath', 'meanwhile' JOHN/4:31): render 'between' throughout or add an alternate — decide at PR3.
LXX ἀνὰ μέσον [LXX unverified] is a phrase, not a lemma pair.

entries.rationale: Call / name / summon / cry out (689 verses); GEN/1:5 naming. YLT 'call' ~565. Pair: LXX GEN/1:5 ἐκάλεσεν [LXX unverified].
notes: Also 'read' (~32 verses: DEUT/17:19, NEHE/8:8 — reading aloud is calling out the text) and 'proclaim' (~57). 'read' could be an alternate, but it is ἀναγινώσκω's natural claim (29 NT verses) and cannot be shared. Decide: 'call' throughout, or own 'read' here and give ἀναγινώσκω another term.

entries.rationale: YLT 'day' 1869/1930; ἡμέρα 356/368. Pair: LXX GEN/1:5 [LXX unverified].
YLT 'night' 219/223; νύξ 58/58. Pair: LXX GEN/1:5 [LXX unverified].
YLT 'evening/even' 125/125; ἑσπέρα 3 NT verses (LUKE/24:29). Pair: LXX GEN/1:5 [LXX unverified].
notes: Homonym erev H6154 ('mixed multitude'/'woof') is a separate Strong's number — not covered. 'between the evenings' (EX/12:6) renders compositionally.

entries.rationale: YLT 'morning' 185/189. Paired noun-to-noun with πρωΐα (MATT/27:1, JOHN/21:4).
notes: LXX GEN/1:5 uses the adverb πρωΐ [LXX unverified]; NT πρωΐ (12 verses) then takes a distinct term ('early') under I2.

entries.rationale: Cardinal 'one' — GEN/1:5 'day one' is cardinal, not ordinal (YLT keeps it); DEUT/6:4 'Yahweh is one'. 'first' is rishon H7223 / πρῶτος's claim, so echad never takes 'first': the NT 'first day of the week' (μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων, JOHN/20:1) becomes 'one of the sabbaths', preserving the GEN/1:5 echo (P2).
notes: YLT 'first' in 39 H259 verses and 14 εἷς verses — those move to 'one'.
